3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Today, the management of FC Anrica had invited me to attend a pivotal football match. At Lucian's urging, I accepted.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: The team was representing Sordland in the international arena. According to Lucian, it would have been un-presidential not to put in an appearance.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: Today, the management of FC Anrica had invited me to attend a pivotal football match. As a board member, I couldn't reject it. I had to be there at this significant moment for my team.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: We made our way towards the Maroon Stadium. The arena was situated in one of the most crowded quarters of Anrica, surrounded by dense urban development.

10.speaker: Lucian Galade
10.text: "Sir. The security gave us the clear."

11.speaker: Lucian Galade
11.text: "Even just the fact that you are here will surely help with our campaign image."

14.speaker: Player
14.text: "I'm just here to support my team."

18.speaker: Player
18.text: "I just hope FC Gelsord fans don't hold it against me."

20.speaker: Narrator
20.text: I followed the security. We entered beneath a giant sign that read: "Welcome to the Hall of Martyrs."

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text: And of course, all presidents of Sordland -- current and former -- were invited to watch the historic competition.

25.speaker: Narrator
25.text: I was told that my predecessor, Ewald Alphonso, would be joining me in the lounge reserved for us.

26.speaker: Narrator
26.text: I was told that both Tarquin Soll and Ewald Alphonso would be joining me in the lounge reserved for us.

27.speaker: Lucian Galade
27.text: "Please follow the guards to the top floor. You will be seated in the VIP lounge."

28.speaker: Player
28.text: "Are you sure you can't join me?"

30.speaker: Player
30.text: "That's a pity. I'll save you some snacks."

31.speaker: Player
31.text: "I hope there won't be another surprise today."

35.speaker: Player
35.text: "I'm still not sure if this is the right thing to do so soon after the attempt on my life."

36.speaker: Lucian Galade
36.text: "Try not to worry, sir. The security detail has assured me that they have everything under control."

37.speaker: Lucian Galade
37.text: "No, sir. The main VIP lounge has been reserved for presidents only today."

39.speaker: Lucian Galade
39.text: "You know the guests of honor more than I do, sir. If all else fails, just focus on the match. It shouldn't be difficult."

40.speaker: Narrator
40.text: The corridors inside were painted almost completely in maroon. Adorning them were various depictions of the Sordish goat and numerous jerseys, awards and team photographs.

44.speaker: Narrator
44.text: On our way up, I was greeted by the president of the club. Beaming with pride, he immediately shook my hand.

45.speaker: Narrator
45.text: After delivering his best wishes, he kindly pointed us towards the corridor and told me that I could visit the team before the match if I wished to do so.

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: After delivering his best wishes, he kindly pointed us towards the lounge, which was surrounded by heavily armed men.

47.speaker: Narrator
47.text: Once I finally found myself inside, I was greeted by an amazing view of the entire pitch through floor-to-ceiling windows.

51.speaker: Narrator
51.text: I took a seat on the leather sofa and watched as the action began.

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: FC Anrica was finally in the Merkopan Champions Cup -- the most prestigious football tournament in the world. For the first time ever, a Sordish team had managed to qualify for the Knockout phase.

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: They were representing Sordland in the international arena. I couldn't help but feel a surge of pride as Lucian and I headed to the stadium.

54.speaker: Narrator
54.text: Millions of Sordish people were waiting to watch FC Anrica compete against the legendary Rizian team Real Montaklar. Despite all odds being stacked against the team, the mood was full of hope.

55.speaker: Narrator
55.text: A win today would bring Anrica to the quarter finals, a feat that no Sordish team had ever managed to achieve.

56.speaker: Narrator
56.text: Another group of fans raised their boards to reveal a silhouette of the famous Hall of Warriors -- a Markian-era architectural ruin in Anrica -- with Tarquin Soll in front of it.

57.speaker: Narrator
57.text: The stadium erupted in applause as the players started coming out onto the field.

58.speaker: Narrator
58.text: Right after the referee signalled the start of the match, the door behind us closed with a thud.

64.speaker: Lucian Galade
64.text: "Sir. The security gave us the clear and informed us that Tarquin Soll has already arrived at the lounge."

67.speaker: Lucian Galade
67.text: "Don't fret, sir. Today is a day to relax. Perhaps even celebrate."

68.speaker: Narrator
68.text: Lucian's pocket radio crackled. After responding, he turned to me.

69.speaker: Lucian Galade
69.text: "Good luck. I know he's quite the imposing presence."

70.speaker: Narrator
70.text: Behind him, Mayor Curtan Leste and Gus Manger were waiting to greet me as well. All of them had FC Anrica pins attached to their collars.

71.speaker: Narrator
71.text: As the players of Real Montaklar lined up in the middle of the field, FC Anrica fans started chanting: "We'll eat you whole for Colonel Soll!"

72.speaker: Narrator
72.text: As we wound our way through the streets, I noticed the name of Tarquin Soll everywhere. Since I'd last been here, markets, restaurants and even pubs named after the Colonel had all popped up.

73.speaker: Player
73.text: "Why is Anrica so crazy about Soll all of a sudden?"

74.speaker: Player
74.text: "It seems like Mayor Curtan Leste isn't following our de-Sollinization policy."

84.speaker: Player
84.text: "Did this all happen after his death?"

85.speaker: Player
85.text: "Is it just me or are they really using the name of a criminal everywhere?"

86.speaker: Player
86.text: "Am I imagining things, or did we just pass a pub called 'Alco-Soll'?"

91.speaker: Lucian Galade
91.text: "I've heard it is part of an ad campaign for Anrica. An attempt to draw tourists, or at least Sollist ones, to the city. Soll's legacy still lives on for millions, after all."

94.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
94.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Admin_Monica_Barred"] == false  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Personal_Festival_Force"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Personal_Festival_LesteKicked"] == true)) == false

98.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
98.text: "It looks like it's working well for the city. And if you moved back home, I'm sure you'd get free meals and drinks everywhere you went."

99.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
99.text: "I doubt the Colonel would approve of his name being used as a tourist draw. But he's not around anymore, is he?"

100.speaker: Narrator
100.text: Ewald Alphonso quickly walked up to me, shook my hand and sat next to me with a grin.

101.speaker: Narrator
101.text: Ewald Alphonso quickly walked up to the sofa, shook our hands and sat next to us, smiling as he did so.

102.speaker: Tarquin Soll
102.text: "Ha. You know, I never had a strong connection to this place. Mr. Leste should have asked my permission before using my name to market his city."

103.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
103.text: "Oh, it was actually Gus Manger's idea."

105.speaker: Gus Manger
105.text: "And all of Sordland! Never before has a Sordish team reached this stage in the Merkopan Cup."

106.speaker: Tarquin Soll
106.text: "Why am I not surprised? He's full of ideas, your Mr. Manger, except when it comes to the job he's actually supposed to be doing."

107.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
107.text: "No need to be so dismissive. Gus has proven himself time and again. His work rejuvenated Sordish industries. And without him, Anrica wouldn't be the city it is today."

108.speaker: Player
108.text: "Honestly, working with Gus has been nothing but a disaster."

109.speaker: Player
109.text: "I must say, Gus has been a very valuable minister of my cabinet."

112.speaker: Tarquin Soll
112.text: "Just what we need. Another president in thrall to Mr. Manger and his get-rich-quick schemes."

113.speaker: Tarquin Soll
113.text: "All of the man's so-called accomplishments have been purely accidental."

114.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
114.text: "He invested heavily in this city and helped transform Anrica into a tourist destination. And he's the one who saw the potential in football."

115.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
115.text: "You say that, Mr. Soll, but Mr. Manger is a respectable professional who actually loves this country."

116.speaker: Tarquin Soll
116.text: "More like an errand boy, doing the bidding of those who line his pockets."

118.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
118.text: "I don't intend to take on the role of his personal spokesman."

119.speaker: Narrator
119.text: As if on cue, Real Montaklar's defense made a crucial block, sending the ball back down the field.

120.speaker: Narrator
120.text: Just then, FC Anrica's star midfielder made a breakaway down the field. The crowd erupted into cheers as the ball was passed from player to player, each touch bringing it closer to the goal.

121.speaker: Tarquin Soll
121.text: "Too predictable. They won't make it past the other team's defense."

123.speaker: Player
123.text: "Are you a Real Montaklar supporter, Colonel?"

124.speaker: Player
124.text: "With your strategy skills, you should be a football coach, Colonel."

125.speaker: Player
125.text: "They'll get it next time. Have some faith in our team."

129.speaker: Player
129.text: "My boys will win this. You'll see."

130.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
130.text: "You know, it was actually Gus Manger's idea. Turning Anrica into the city of Soll."

131.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
131.text: "Without him, Anrica wouldn't be the city it is today. But his instincts may have failed him with this ill-timed strategy."

132.speaker: Player
132.text: "Honestly, working with Gus has been nothing but a disaster."

133.speaker: Player
133.text: "Maybe it's not such ill timing. Soll's name has been on everyone's lips since the trial."

135.speaker: Player
135.text: "Gus must realize he's aiding Soll's cult of personality with stunts like this."

136.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
136.text: "He invested heavily in this city and helped transform Anrica into a tourist destination. And he saw the potential of football."

137.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
137.text: "Don't be so dismissive. He really is a respectable professional who loves this country."

138.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
138.text: "You make a good point. Maybe Gus' business instincts have rubbed off on you."

139.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
139.text: "Anyway, we didn't come here to talk about Mr. Manger. We're here to watch our men win."

144.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
144.text: "How about you, Mr. Rayne? It's been a while since we last met."

151.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
151.text: "How are you holding up after that attack at the parade?"

152.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
152.text: "I heard your man Serge gave his life to protect you... My condolences. He was a true champion."

153.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
153.text: "Is everything going well at the Palace?"

154.speaker: Narrator
154.text: As if on cue, Real Montaklar's defense made a crucial block, sending the ball back down the field.

155.speaker: Player
155.text: "I didn't know you were a football fan, Mr. Alphonso."

156.speaker: Player
156.text: "They'll get it next time. Have some faith in our team."

160.speaker: Player
160.text: "My boys will win this. You'll see."

162.speaker: Player
162.text: "They're against the top team in Eastern Merkopa. It won't be so easy."

165.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
165.text: "Honestly, I'm more of a money fan. Football is the future, you'll see."

168.speaker: Player
168.text: "I'm trying my best to stay calm. Thank you."

169.speaker: Player
169.text: "Honestly, I'm worried. The country is showing signs of instability again."

170.speaker: Player
170.text: "It would be a lie if I said it's been great."

172.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
172.text: "Yes, Mr. Rayne. Sordish politics is getting complicated again. You have to be careful."

177.speaker: Tarquin Soll
177.text: "Take on the responsibility for once, Mr. Rayne."

178.speaker: Tarquin Soll
178.text: "You've had the authority for four years."

179.speaker: Narrator
179.text: Suddenly, a huge roar shook the stadium. The crowd was in a frenzy as FC Anrica finally got the ball past the dominating Rizian defenders.

180.speaker: Narrator
180.text: Just then, Montaklar midfielders executed an incredibly fast counter-attack, scoring a goal that put them ahead in just a few seconds.

181.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
181.text: "It was bad luck getting a top-tier Rizian team as our opponent."

182.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
182.text: "I still applaud our guys for giving their best. Not even FC Gelsord has ever come this far in an international tournament. "

183.speaker: Player
183.text: "Why so bleak? It's not even half time yet. Anrica can still come out on top."

184.speaker: Player
184.text: "Yes. Football is like politics. Sometimes it's all about luck."

185.speaker: Player
185.text: "Don't overestimate FC Gelsord. We already broke their record and took the title. Times are changing."

189.speaker: Player
189.text: "Honestly, I don't really care about any of this."

193.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
193.text: "I guess you meant to say money. FC Anrica came this far thanks to our investments."

194.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
194.text: "It's not about luck. It's about money."

196.speaker: Narrator
196.text: The Sordish side of the stadium fell completely silent.

197.speaker: Curtan Leste
197.text: "Mr. President. I didn't expect you to show your support in person."

198.speaker: Curtan Leste
198.text: "Thanks for being here. This match means a lot for all of us Anricans."

199.speaker: Curtan Leste
199.text: "You are always welcome in Anrica, and it is great to see you show support in person."
199.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Admin_Monica_Barred"] == false  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Personal_Festival_Force"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Personal_Festival_LesteKicked"] == true)) == false

200.speaker: Player
200.text: "It is great to be here in Anrica."

201.speaker: Player
201.text: "I have high hopes for today. This is a big achievement for Sordish football."

202.speaker: Player
202.text: "Honestly, I don't know much about football. But I'm here for the players and for my country."

208.speaker: Gus Manger
208.text: "Football is of rapidly expanding importance in Sordland and beyond. It's good that we see the opportunity in it."

213.speaker: Gus Manger
213.text: "Football is of rapidly expanding importance in Sordland and beyond. It's important to see the opportunities in it."

214.speaker: Gus Manger
214.text: "Come on, Mr. President! You own a stake in the club!"

215.speaker: Narrator
215.text: The president of the club walked in, handed us gift bags full of FC Anrica merchandise and gave a speech stressing the importance of today's match.

216.speaker: Player_Italic
216.text: Go to the locker room of FC Anrica.

217.speaker: Narrator
217.text: He personally thanked me for my investment and told me that it wouldn't have been possible to transfer big names to the club without it.

219.speaker: Narrator
219.text: The lounge area was guarded by heavily armed men. They nodded at me to enter.

220.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
220.text: "Let's see if they can keep it up."

221.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
221.text: "You just need to look like you care, Mr. Rayne."

226.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll

228.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
228.text: "Considering that a war with Rumburg is on the horizon, you seem almost too composed and calm."

253.text: "Considering everything that's happened in the last four years, you seem almost too composed and calm, Mr. Rayne."

254.speaker: Player
254.text: "Well, as the president, I have to be. You know how it is, Mr. Former President."

255.speaker: Player
255.text: "Don't worry, it's under control. Everything will fall into place soon."

256.speaker: Player
256.text: "Rumburg may be a massive world power, but nobody should underestimate Sordland. You will see what we are capable of."

257.speaker: Player
257.text: "Don't underestimate the power of the government, Mr. Alphonso."

258.speaker: Player
258.text: "What would you have me do? There's nothing I can do about that anymore."

260.speaker: Player
260.text: "I didn't start this mess. Unlike you, I did everything in my power to fix the situation."

261.speaker: Player
261.text: "The CSP is the right place to be for Sordland."

262.speaker: Player
262.text: "They are our allies now, yes. I'm not scared of them."

264.speaker: Player
264.text: "Do I really look that composed? That's good to know."

265.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
265.text: "You don't need to read between the lines."

267.speaker: Narrator
267.text: The only noise that could be heard from the stadium was shouting from the Rizian side: "Montaklar!"
267.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn09_SollTrial_Guilty_Prison"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn09_SollTrial_Guilty_Death"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Soll_Hates_Alphonso"] == true) == false)

268.speaker: Narrator
268.text: All eyes were glued to the scoreboard as the new score appeared: "FC Anrica 0 - Real Montaklar 1."

276.speaker: Tarquin Soll
276.text: "What you did can only be described as treachery, Mr. Rayne."

277.speaker: Tarquin Soll
277.text: "I can now see that despite everything, Mr. Alphonso here was a much better president."

278.speaker: Narrator
278.text: From that moment on, we turned our complete attention to the match in front of us.

282.speaker: Tarquin Soll
282.text: "Don't expect that to make sense for him. You are talking to Ewald Alphonso."

286.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
286.text: "Sure. I'll be a punching bag for both of you today."

290.speaker: Tarquin Soll
290.text: "Sadly, money is still the only thing you care about."

291.speaker: Narrator
291.text: Suddenly, the ball was passed to the famous Sordish striker, Hakon Zlater, who was in front of the goal. I noticed Soll shifting in his seat, his gaze suddenly locked on the field.

292.speaker: Narrator
292.text: The referee blew the whistle. It was halftime.

293.speaker: Narrator
293.text: We heard a noise from above us. A zeppelin was flying over the stadium with a giant poster hanging beneath it.

300.speaker: Narrator
300.text: The Anrican players already seemed like they had given their all. They looked incredibly stressed and tired.

301.speaker: Narrator
301.text: The Anrican players already seemed like they had given up. They looked incredibly calm, but their movements were slow.

302.speaker: Narrator
302.text: The Rizian players kept dominating the field.

304.speaker: Narrator
304.text: I noticed that it was an advertisement for the Alphonso Foundation. At the center of the poster stood Ewald Alphonso, portrayed with a warm smile and a twinkle in his eye.

305.speaker: Narrator
305.text: In his outstretched hand, he held a whimsical compass, glowing with a soft golden light. Surrounding him were people from all walks of life and cultures.

306.speaker: Narrator
306.text: The tagline, written in elegant and uplifting typography, was prominently displayed at the bottom: "Alphonso Foundation: Bringing Hope To Those In Need, One Act of Kindness at a Time."

307.speaker: Player
307.text: "Now you're asking for donations at football matches? How does a non-profit even afford this ad?"

311.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
311.text: "I'm doing my best to increase our exposure and to help the homeless of this country. This isn't some commercial advertisement."

312.speaker: Narrator
312.text: Just then, the speakers in the stadium started playing a sound recording in full volume.

314.speaker: Narrator
314.text: "Ladies and gentlemen, we bring you a message from the Alphonso Foundation, dedicated to spreading kindness and hope to the less fortunate."

315.speaker: Narrator
315.text: "Picture a Sordland where compassion shines brighter than the stars in the night sky, where the power of generosity uplifts those who need it most. That Sordland can exist, thanks to the Alphonso Foundation."

316.speaker: Narrator
316.text: "Led by the charismatic and esteemed President Ewald Alphonso, this foundation is on a mission to make a difference in the lives of our fellow citizens, one act of kindness at a time."

317.speaker: Narrator
317.text: "Every Sordish Ren you donate to the Alphonso Foundation helps us provide shelter, food, and a chance for a brighter future to those without a home, without hope."

318.speaker: Narrator
318.text: "Thanks to the donations of President Ewald Alphonso and thousands of Sordish citizens, the Alphonso Foundation has already lifted hundreds out of homelessness."

325.speaker: Narrator
325.text: "Thanks to the donations of President Ewald Alphonso, and esteemed figures like President Anton Rayne, as well as thousands of Sordish citizens, the Alphonso Foundation has already lifted thousands out of homelessness."
325.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn04_FoundationDonation_LargeSum"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn04_FoundationDonation_LargeSum"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn04_FoundationDonation_SmallSum"] == true)

326.speaker: Narrator
326.text: "Won't you join us in this noble endeavor? Just call the number, 1-600-ALPHONSO, to make your contribution today. Your support will help us extend a helping hand to those in need."

327.speaker: Narrator
327.text: The recording ended with a few seconds of upbeat jazzy background music that slowly faded out.

328.speaker: Player
328.text: "I appreciate the credit, but you didn't need to put my name in there."

332.speaker: Player
332.text: "It's good to see that you're at least helping the poor in some way. That is commendable."

333.speaker: Player
333.text: "I'll be honest. I think that ad was a little distasteful."

337.speaker: Player
337.text: "You don't even live here anymore. I'm surprised you'd think an ad like this would work."

340.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
340.text: "Why wouldn't it? Don't act like I'm no longer Sordish. I was also a president of this republic, Anton."

352.speaker: Tarquin Soll
352.text: "You had your whole term to plan affordable housing programs. Instead, you decided to pass the buck to Mr. Rayne here."

353.speaker: Tarquin Soll
353.text: "Is this your way of personal redemption -- spending a few Rens out of your billions and portraying yourself as their saviour?"

357.speaker: Tarquin Soll
357.text: "A couple of hundred people? Congratulations to you both. This is how Sordland will eradicate poverty."

361.speaker: Tarquin Soll
361.text: "You too, Mr. Rayne? I thought you would see through this scheme."

366.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
366.text: "Unlike you, Mr. Soll, I'm not portraying myself as a hero here. I retired from politics just like you did, and I'm now using my clout to help the poor. What's so wrong about this?"

367.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
367.text: "Unlike Soll, I'm trying to use my retirement to make a change. I believe there's a lot of value in using my clout to generate money for those in need."

368.speaker: Tarquin Soll
368.text: "You know I never called myself a hero, Ewald. It was my supporters who portrayed me as one. Don't spin the truth."

369.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
369.text: "Maybe they didn't have any other choice back then."

370.speaker: Tarquin Soll
370.text: "Are you still sore about the party giving you a hard time after I left? Admit it, Ewald. You never could accept being a less popular leader. You hated living under the shadow of what I built."

371.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
371.text: "It is true. I did hate working inside your shadow empire. But I succeeded in dismantling a lot of those obstacles you laid out for me, and opened the way for reforms. But you never let the party go free."

375.speaker: Player
375.text: "You know I'm not going to take that response at face value. But regardless, I really hope your intentions are genuine."

376.speaker: Player
376.text: "As much as I respect that, I don't believe an issue like this can be left to the *kindness* of the wealthy."

377.speaker: Player
377.text: "And I support your endeavors on that."

378.speaker: Player
378.text: "You don't need to explain or justify, Ewald. I get the idea already."

381.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
381.text: "Oh no. Is that a Malenyevist talking point? I guess we have to agree to disagree."

385.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
385.text: "Oh. I almost forgot about your heavy shift towards Malenyevism. I guess I will just stop right here and we have to agree to disagree."

386.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
386.text: "They are, Mr. Rayne. You can be sure of it."

387.speaker: Player
387.text: "Is that even true, Mr. Soll? Are you really denying that you did nothing to construct a cult of personality?"

388.speaker: Player
388.text: "Nobody had any choice. There was no other option."

389.speaker: Player
389.text: "Despite everything, we can't deny the millions of people who loved and respected Mr. Soll. That is the reality."

391.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
391.text: "Precisely my point. Would you say it is a valid choice if you only had one option to pick from?"

392.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
392.text: "I'm not saying otherwise. But I must remind you, those same people also stood in the way of progress."

393.speaker: Tarquin Soll
393.text: "What does it matter? You believed in that so much that you already ordered the removal of my face from public places, haven't you?"

394.speaker: Tarquin Soll
394.text: "So it was I who controlled each and every member? I was behind every problem you faced within the USP? Do you really believe that?"

395.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
395.text: "I still remember how the party became divided after you stopped supporting me. It is on them for being blind to the progress we were making."

396.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
396.text: "You are the founder of the party, Mr. Soll. Don't even try to deny your influence over it."

397.speaker: Player
397.text: "What do you mean? Mr. Soll supported you after the congress?"

398.speaker: Player
398.text: "Sollists still make up the bulk of the USP today. Everybody is aware of your influence, Mr. Soll."

399.speaker: Tarquin Soll
399.text: "Instead of blaming the party, why don't you take a look at yourself? That same party voted me out on their own volition in preference of *you*."

400.speaker: Tarquin Soll
400.text: "According to you, their only *correct* decision must have been to elect *you* as leader. And the rest are completely wrong. Do you think everything is a problem that is specifically created to block *you*?"

401.speaker: Player
401.text: "Gentlemen. Why don't we calm down a little? We are here to watch football."

403.speaker: Narrator
403.text: Neither of the two men seemed to care. They continued without stopping to hear what I said.

404.speaker: Tarquin Soll
404.text: "Instead of blaming the party, why don't you take a look at yourselves? That same party has voted me out on their own volition in preference of the likes of *you*."

405.speaker: Tarquin Soll
405.text: "Take a look at yourself. You are the personification of what you're trying to criticize."

406.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
406.text: "Briefly, yes. The last couple years until I became president in '49, he pushed several of my plans through. And I thought he believed in my vision."

407.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
407.text: "But it was all to get credit for initiating the reforms, wasn't it? That was the only way to save Sollism for you."

409.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
409.text: "You were already voted out by your own followers and your term was ending in a few years. You couldn't afford to go against the current."

410.speaker: Tarquin Soll
410.text: "You're being ingrateful, Ewald. I agreed to your reforms to help smooth the transition of power."

411.speaker: Player
411.text: "I remember Soll's reforms but I still remember those years as being very unstable."

413.speaker: Player
413.text: "Are you saying Mr. Soll's reforms between '46 and '49 were actually your plans?"

414.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
414.text: "Of course, they were. It was the Sollists that portrayed it differently."

415.speaker: Narrator
415.text: He looked Tarquin Soll in the eye.

416.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
416.text: "My wing and I pushed for those reforms. Soll merely approved them."

417.speaker: Player
417.text: "You have a point, Mr. Soll. But don't act like you're above all of us."

418.speaker: Player
418.text: "That's an empty argument. The party and the government were in that state due to your actions over 20 years."

419.speaker: Player
419.text: "This is getting out of hand. I think both of you should calm down."

420.speaker: Player
420.text: "Oh, please. We know that you are still trying to pull the strings behind the scenes, Mr. Soll."

421.speaker: Tarquin Soll
421.text: "Correct. They built a republic within two decades in the harshest political climate, and they reached a state of being able to elect and oust their own leaders."

422.speaker: Tarquin Soll
422.text: "Oh, what a disastrous state to be in."

423.speaker: Narrator
423.text: He waved a dismissive hand, as if to brush away the notion.

427.speaker: Tarquin Soll
427.text: "I can see now that both of you have only brought disaster to Sordland."

429.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
429.text: "What do you mean? They just scored."

433.speaker: Tarquin Soll
433.text: "Not a punching bag. You deserve to be in prison for your deal with the Rums."

441.speaker: Tarquin Soll
441.text: "No donation can redeem your betrayal to this country."

445.speaker: Tarquin Soll
445.text: "I didn't need to build a cult for myself, Mr. Rayne. I built a republic."

446.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
446.text: "Mr. Rayne has a point, Mr. Soll."

448.speaker: Narrator
448.text: Tarquin Soll locked his gaze at Ewald.

449.speaker: Tarquin Soll
449.text: "I did not believe in your *vision*, but I truly wished for your success -- for the sake of Sordland."

450.speaker: Tarquin Soll
450.text: "But soon after your destruction of our economy, I realized how naive I was to open that gate for you."

451.speaker: Narrator
451.text: Suddenly, we turned our heads to the field as a massive roar shook the stadium.

454.speaker: Narrator
454.text: The second half was already in full swing and Anrican players were aggressively attacking, weaving in and out of defenders with speed.

455.speaker: Narrator
455.text: The Sordish crowd went crazy as Zlater's powerful shot brought the ball to the back of the Rizian net.

462.speaker: Player
462.text: "Are you always this negative, Mr. Soll?"

463.speaker: Tarquin Soll
463.text: "I'm a realist, Mr. Rayne. I don't have time for fake positivities."

464.speaker: Narrator
464.text: Suddenly, the cheering was interrupted by the linesman raising the flag -- making an offside call.

465.speaker: Narrator
465.text: Anrican fans dominated the stadium as the scoreboard was replaced with the new score: "FC Anrica 1 - Real Montaklar 1."

467.speaker: Player
467.text: "That referee is trying to sabotage us. He was clearly in front of the defenders when he received the ball."

468.speaker: Player
468.text: "Do you think the Rizians could have bought the referees?"

471.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
471.text: "That was a great comeback. We can still make it."

475.speaker: Tarquin Soll
475.text: "Halt your endless bickering. The linesman made the right call."

480.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
480.text: "It's your own club, Mr. Rayne. But suit yourself."

481.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
481.text: "Well... They have the prestige and the money to do that."

482.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
482.text: "The angle was all wrong. A decision like that shouldn't be made without proper evaluation."

483.speaker: Tarquin Soll
483.text: "What next? You're going to install cameras and analyze every position from different angles?"

491.speaker: Player
491.text: "The Global Football Association is clearly biased against us."

492.speaker: Player
492.text: "What next? You're going to install cameras and analyze every position from different angles?"

494.speaker: Player
494.text: "You should have more faith in our Sordish players."

495.speaker: Player
495.text: "Exactly. We can be the underdogs here, but we cannot let the Rizians intimidate us."

496.speaker: Narrator
496.text: The excitement in the stadium reached a fever pitch as the Sordish striker dribbled the ball past two defenders and took a shot at the goal again. The crowd held its breath as the ball sailed through the air, but the Montaklar goalkeeper made a miraculous save.

503.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
503.text: "It's your own club, Mr. Rayne. But suit yourself."

504.speaker: Narrator
504.text: The excitement in the stadium reached a fever pitch as the Rizian striker dribbled the ball past two defenders and took a shot at the goal. The crowd held its breath as the ball sailed through the air, but the Anrican goalkeeper made a miraculous save.

505.speaker: Narrator
505.text: As the last minutes of the match kicked in, we found ourselves falling more and more silent.

545.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Archetype_SollistRayne"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn09_EnT_SordishRecovery"] == true  or  (Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EducationReform"] == false)) == false

550.speaker: Player
550.text: "I wish Serge could have lived to see this day."

551.speaker: Lucian Galade
551.text: "Truly a tragedy, sir. I know the pain is still fresh."

555.speaker: Player
555.text: "I can't believe Petr's not here to see this."

556.speaker: Lucian Galade
556.text: "A tragedy, sir. Mr. Vectern did excel at making public appearances, if nothing else."

557.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
557.text: "Well, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}? What do you think about the city's new marketing plan?"

558.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
558.text: "Well, Colonel? How do you feel about being Anrica's new poster boy?"

559.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
559.text: "You and I both know Gus. His only allegiance is to his own bank account."

560.speaker: Player
560.text: "Mr. Alphonso. How have you been since the trial?"

561.speaker: Player
561.text: "No, he certainly isn't. I saw to that myself."

562.speaker: Player
562.text: "Alphonso. We have unfinished business, don't we?"

567.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
567.text: "What's unfinished about it? I'd say the Gasom affair wrapped up well for the both of us."

568.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
568.text: "I've been just fine, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}. I wish I could say the same for my company."

572.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
572.text: "I do wonder if the trial was the right idea. It hasn't done much to diminish his outsized legacy."

573.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
573.text: "You were so invested in getting him out of the picture. A pity you weren't as invested in other matters."

574.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
574.text: "Honestly, I've never been better. It feels as if a huge weight has been lifted."

581.speaker: Narrator
581.text: It was a group of Anricans who were holding signs that read: "FC Anrica Stands Against Rayne!"

582.speaker: Narrator
582.text: Another massive sign displayed the words: "Soldiers! Leave Your Barracks! Save Your Colonel's Dignity!"

586.speaker: Narrator
586.text: Another massive sign displayed the words: "Soldiers! Leave Your Barracks! Avenge Your Colonel!"

587.speaker: Narrator
587.text: Another massive sign displayed the words: "Bring Rayne To Justice!"

588.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
588.text: "They need to be arrested for putting up such signs."

589.speaker: Tarquin Soll
589.text: "At least you still have the support of somebody."

590.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
590.text: "They need to be arrested for putting up such signs."

592.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
592.text: "Looks like the impeachment case did not damage your football career."

593.speaker: Tarquin Soll
593.text: "This football craze seems to have numbed the Anricans a little too much."

594.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
594.text: "Looks like the impeachment case has already lost you the football fans."

595.speaker: Narrator
595.text: Behind them, a poster was being displayed with my and Lileas Graf's faces. I was portrayed wearing an FC Anrica jersey, while Lileas was displayed as an FC Arvory supporter -- her face crossed off with a red marker.

596.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
596.text: "Looks like FC Anrica fans are really into politics. It's good that they're embracing you."

597.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
597.text: "Looks like FC Anrica fans are really into politics. But unfortunately not into you."

598.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
598.text: "It seems like Anricans like you a lot."

599.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
599.text: "It really seems like Anrica is going to be lost to the NFP in the local elections, doesn't it?"

600.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
600.text: "They're promoting the NFP in football matches now. What a time to be alive."

602.speaker: Player
602.text: "What does that supposed to mean, Mr. Soll?"

604.speaker: Player
604.text: "Funny. Do you not see the millions behind me?"

605.speaker: Player
605.text: "Right. At least that's going good for me."

606.speaker: Player
606.text: "The Colonel is right. They are free to express themselves."

607.speaker: Player
607.text: "These are some very dangerous signs. How were they even allowed inside with them?"

608.speaker: Player
608.text: "Is this your doing too, Mr. Soll?"

609.speaker: Player
609.text: "Right. At least that's going good for me."

610.speaker: Player
610.text: "Why don't you both mind your own business, gentlemen? I am already aware of the trial, alright?"

612.speaker: Player
612.text: "There's nothing I can do about that now."

615.speaker: Player
615.text: "If they're choosing Lileas over me, their opinions don't even matter."

617.speaker: Player
617.text: "Well, to be fair, I like Anricans a lot too."

618.speaker: Player
618.text: "What does that supposed to mean, Mr. Soll?"

620.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
620.text: "Looks like Rizians are also scared of a possible war between us and Rumburg."

621.speaker: Tarquin Soll
621.text: "The Toras family is a puppet of Queen Livingston. If the queen wants war, Rizians will follow them."

622.speaker: Tarquin Soll
622.text: "You lost the support of the mechanisms that matter. And you know that doesn't comprise FC Anrica fans."

625.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
625.text: "The contents of that expression seems to be extremely harsh. But suit yourself."

626.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
626.text: "It is you they're targeting after all."

627.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
627.text: "To be fair, this type of statements are not that uncommon in Anrica."

629.speaker: Tarquin Soll
629.text: "You think I'd install a few men with signs to get your attention?"

631.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
631.text: "Sure. And good luck with that. I didn't mean anything bad with it."

632.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
632.text: "You're right. And good luck with that. I didn't mean anything bad with it."

639.speaker: Tarquin Soll
639.text: "You know what it means, Anton. Does everything need to be explained to you in complete detail for you to understand such a basic concept?"

641.speaker: Narrator
641.text: Suddenly, a wave of shouting made us focus back on the field. An Anrican player was shown a yellow card.

645.speaker: Narrator
645.text: With only a few minutes left on the clock, it looked as though the match would end in a draw.

646.speaker: Narrator
646.text: With only a few minutes left on the clock, it looked as though the match would end with a 1-0 loss for FC Anrica.

647.speaker: Narrator
647.text: But suddenly, everything changed. Number 10 of Real Montaklar dribbled expertly towards the goal and effortlessly scored as Anrican defenders watched him in shock.

651.speaker: Narrator
651.text: We watched in silence as the scoreboard was modified to display: "FC Anrica: 0 - Real Montaklar: 2."

652.speaker: Narrator
652.text: But suddenly, everything changed. Number 10 of Real Montaklar dribbled expertly towards the goal and effortlessly scored as Anrican defenders watched him in shock.

653.speaker: Narrator
653.text: But suddenly, everything changed. The Nibiyan star striker Leon al-Ogwaldo dribbled expertly towards the goal and effortlessly scored a goal from an incredible distance as Rizian defenders watched him in shock.

655.speaker: Narrator
655.text: I noticed Tarquin Soll shifting in his seat and a large smile appeared on his face -- one that I had never seen before.

656.speaker: Narrator
656.text: We watched in silence as the scoreboard was modified to display: "FC Anrica 1 - Real Montaklar: 2."

658.speaker: Narrator
658.text: We stood up and watched the scoreboard change to: "FC Anrica 2 - Real Montaklar: 1."

660.speaker: Player
660.text: "You're right. They're clearly asking the military to intervene. This cannot be allowed."

663.speaker: Player
663.text: "These are some very dangerous signs. How were they even allowed inside with them?"

665.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
665.text: "Why not? You already went too deep by prosecuting the *hero* of the republic."

667.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
667.text: "Anrica is full of people like this these days."

669.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
669.text: "I'd be extremely careful if I were you."

670.speaker: Narrator
670.text: The Rizian side broke into massive applause as the referee blew the final whistle.

671.speaker: Narrator
671.text: The Sordish side broke into massive applause as the referee blew the final whistle.

675.speaker: Player
675.text: "They're just a bunch of hippies. Who cares what they say?"

677.speaker: Player
677.text: "Do you think Rizia would aid Rumburg in a war with us?"

678.speaker: Player
678.text: "Well, they're right. Nobody wants a war with Rumburg."

684.speaker: Tarquin Soll
684.text: "You must go congratulate them in person, Mr. Rayne."

688.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
688.text: "That's unbelievable. We should go down and congratulate the boys in person."

689.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
689.text: "Yes. This is an historic win. I'll come with you."

690.speaker: Narrator
690.text: We left the lounge and went downstairs to congratulate the team of FC Anrica on their massive win against Real Montaklar.

691.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
691.text: "We should go down and console the boys."

692.speaker: Narrator
692.text: We left the lounge and went downstairs to congratulate the team for their efforts.

701.speaker: Narrator
701.text: Suddenly, the ball was passed to the famous Sordish striker, Hakon Zlater, who was in front of the goal.

705.speaker: Tarquin Soll
705.text: "Now Rayne is offering proper housing assistance while you waste your time on crap like this."

706.speaker: Tarquin Soll
706.text: "And now you're wasting your time on crap like this."
